chemistry.text: You make your way over to Gemini and take a seat. She seems like a smart student; maybe she can help you through this class.
As you approach, her emerald eyes stare away from you and lock onto the front of the classroom, almost purposefully.

chemistry.name: Professor Hermit
chemistry.text: Well, if everyone has found a partner, let’s get on with today’s class.

chemistry.name: Professor Hermit
chemistry.text: Today, we’re going to be doing an iodine clock oscillator experiment to get you all excited for the semester.

chemistry.name: Professor Hermit
chemistry.text: Our lovely Gemini prepared 3 types of solutions for each table. Go ahead and grab one of each.
Before you can even try to move, Gemini gets up and returns with 3 solutions. She sheepishly sits back down.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Hey, umm… I’m Gemini. It’s uh, nice to meet you. I got us one of each.
She nervously looks away again.

chemistry.name: Professor Hermit
chemistry.text: Alright, class, settle down. Now that everyone has acquired the samples, go ahead and turn on the stir plates in front of you.

chemistry.name: Professor Hermit
chemistry.text: You’re going to quickly combine solutions A, B, and C into the beaker in front of you. Then, note down what happens.
You turn on the stir plate.
Gemini’s nervousness seems to fade a bit as she becomes more immersed in science.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: I’m adding the potassium iodate and sulfuric acid, now. Can you grab solution B?

options.text: Empty the beaker on the stir plate into the second beaker

chemistry.text: You want to be a helpful lab partner. Despite being a little lost at her earlier statement, you hand her solution B as she asked.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Thanks, you’re a pretty helpful lab partner.
Gemini looks over at you.

She opens her mouth and starts talking about the solution, but her voice starts to mumble and drop off as she blushes, realizing she must’ve sounded like an absolute dork while spouting off the chemicals.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: *Ahem* Well, I’m going to start adding in the second solution.
She’s clearly off-balance now. While she’s adding in the second solution, you proactively grab the third solution and hand it to her as well.
Your action seems to put her a little at ease as her fears of being seen as a science freak fade a little.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Oh, perfect, I was just about to ask you for it, but you’re already on top of it.
Your hands brush for a moment as she grasps it from you and adds it to the stir plate.
She seems to be a little uptight, so you grab the beaker off the stir plate and pour it into solution B.
Her mouth hangs open as you do so. She’s confounded by your actions. Is it a power move? Some sort of rebellion?
Whatever it is, Gemini seems very displeased by your actions, although it does seem to have broken her out of her shell a little.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Why did you just do that? I mean, it’s not like that changes anything, but still, why?

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Well, whatever. I can do this lab by myself anyway.
Gemini moves the mixed solution back onto the stir plate, keeping a careful eye for any more of your shenanigans as she pours in the third beaker.

chemistry.skip: The chemistry is intriguing, and you want to know more about it. You ask her what she knows about the solutions out of genuine curiosity, remembering how she was helping the teacher earlier.

chemistry.text: She seems taken aback that you’re asking about it, which quickly forms into a sweet smile.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Really? You wanna know more? Umm, okay. I’ve been doing chemistry since I was a little shape. I’d be happy to teach you more!
You hand her solution B.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: This one is a starch solution with malonic acid and manganese sulfate.
Gemini quickly and precisely pours solution B into the beaker and grabs solution C. Gemini looks over at you, realizing you might not be following.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Don’t worry if this is a bit complex for you at the moment. I didn’t understand a lot of what was going on until my father bought me a chemistry set when I was 12 years old.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Even then, I was just mixing the chemicals to see the fun reactions.
You nod back at her in reassurance.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Okay, and lastly, this one is just hydrogen peroxide. With this added… well, you’ll see what happens.
You watch in stunned silence as the solution quickly turns a dark blue, then back to yellow, and back to dark blue again, alternating between the two colors.
Just as quickly as it alternated, Gemini’s personality seems to have become more confident. She’s practically glowing now.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: It’s pretty cool, right? It’s actually a combination of a radical process and a slower, non-radical process that results in iodide ions and free iodine that form triiodide atoms and… Oh, I just did it again.
Just like the solution before you, her personality has once again alternated. She now seems sheepish and withdrawn.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: I apologize. I just get really worked up about chemistry. It’s been my dream since I was little.
You give her a nod of understanding and let her continue.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Have you heard of Marie Circlie? She won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry and Physics for her work in radiation. My dad used to read me stories about her.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: She’s an icon. I want to be just like her. Someday, I’d even like to win a Nobel Prize.
She leans in closer to the iodine oscillator, staring at it with deep intensity and tranquility beneath her eyes.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: I’ve seen it so many times, but I still can’t get over how beautiful something like this is.
For a brief moment, she seems 100% herself, not shyly apologizing to you or nerding out about the chemistry, just admiring the world around her.
Pretty soon, the moment fades, and she turns to face you. Her eyes still can’t quite meet yours.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: I bet you’re curious how I knew Professor Hermit already? This is actually my first year. Last year, one of my friends started here, and I got to know Professor Hermit when I’d visit her at school.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: So yeah, as you probably already picked up… I’m a bit of a nerd…
She almost mumbles the last bit. Unable to maintain the continuous attention any further, she awkwardly turns away to her notebook, her hands shaking as she holds her pencil.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: We’ve still got the lab report to do...

options.text: Goof off & write in her notebook
Talk about own dreams and ambitions

chemistry.text: Seeing how narrow her attention is on her notebook, you hatch an idea that brings a sly grin to your face. Along the header area, you start to sketch a cool S, then a little space guy.
You start doodling a weird face when she looks up and catches you in the act.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: What the? That’s uncalled for, and you did it in pen, too? Thanks a lot for that. I was starting to think that you were kinda cool.
Gemini flips her notebook to the next page and restarts on her lab report.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Whatever, just do your lab report, too. Let me know if you need any help with it.
She angles herself away from you, making sure you can’t easily access any part of her notebook. Resigned, you grab your own notebook from your backpack and start on the report, too.
After a bit, Gemini glances over her shoulder at you working diligently. She nods at you silently and keeps working.
Her genuineness touched you. In return, you decided to tell her your own plans. Her eyes widen at you, focused intently on your eyes for the first time. Gemini’s eyes glimmer; her body relaxes.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: That’s quite something, huh? Thanks for sharing. It makes me feel a lot better about sharing my own lofty dreams.
Her eyes soften

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: And you know what? I think you should go for it, regardless of what anyone might say to you.
The twinkle in her eyes fades away as she takes a deep breath.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: I wasn’t really sure of what I wanted. Honestly, I’m still not sure. I owe a good amount to my friend for encouraging me.
A comfortable silence fills the air between you two. A moment later, she angles toward you with her notebook.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Let’s finish the lab report… together.
You pull out your notebook and start answering what you can, asking Gemini occasional questions and talking to her about the experiment.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Right, it’s the imbalance between the processes that causes the oscillations. That’s also why the yellow state lasts for a far shorter time than the deep blue state.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: That’s the fast process, as you can probably surmise.
She seems less worried, simply talking to you about the experiment. Still, you can’t help but feel like something’s bothering her.
You try to ask her about it, but she drowns you out with discussions about the lab. You decide it's best to let it go. Your dual concentrated efforts help you finish before everyone else.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: We make a pretty good team, don’t we? We got done so early.
You compliment her on her effortless genius. That seems to make her slightly uncomfortable, but she’s altogether grateful.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Thanks, you’re plenty smart yourself.
After both of you finish the report, Gemini moves to stand up, but you stand up first, grabbing both of your reports and turning them in at the front of the class

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Oh, thank you very much.
You return to your seat next to her. She looks down at the floor.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Chemistry today was pretty fun. Would you want to be lab partners again next class? … I’m just saying that because you seem pretty capable, and we were able to get it done pretty early!
She turns her attention to the iodine oscillator, which has long since faded. Still, the deep blue is somewhat mesmerizing to look at.
Suddenly, a large BOOM echoes across the room, making you jump. You and Gemini both turn to look at Rowan and his partner, who look guilty. The fire sprinklers engage, drenching the students.
Professor Hermit quickly springs into action, using a shutgun to disengage the sprinklers. Professor Hermit makes his way over to Rowan and begins reprimanding him.
Gemini turns back to the table. She talks in a slightly hushed tone.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: I feel somewhat bad for him. He’s a good kid, but he’s always been one to cause these sorts of things. He means well, though.
She fidgets nervously in her seat, uncertain of what to do. Her body shakes, but her mind is frozen, not thinking very clearly.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Do you think we should go over and help him?

options.text: Ignore Rowan & engage Gemini in chemistry
Pry Gemini to learn about Rowan's past mistakes
Head over to Rowan and help console him

chemistry.text: Well, it might seem cruel, but you decided the best thing to do here is to ignore Rowan so as not to bring him any more shame. You tell this to Gemini.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Well, I guess that makes sense. When I make mistakes like that, it’s nice not to be suffocated by others.
She still looks fidgety, clearly wanting to help in some way. You start talking to her about the periodic table to get her mind off of it.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Huh? The periodic table? I’m a bit embarrassed to admit it, but I don’t actually know all of it… There are a lot of cool elements, though. Like Indium, which you can actually chew.
She understands your intent. While talking about the elements doesn’t truly calm her, she adapts your strategy and frantically spouts the facts she knows to take her mind off of it.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Hydrogen is also super cool. It’s unique in its formation and how it forms bonds.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Besides that, it also has amazing applications for stellar spectroscopy as the most abundant element in the universe. Plus, it actually emits a pretty pink light when you heat it up.
She drones on for a bit. At some point, you lose track of what she’s saying and just nod along with her.
You perk up at the mention of Rowan being an accidental troublemaker and are desperate to know more. Curious, you ask Gemini about past examples.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Really? That’s what you’re focused on in this situation? Don’t you think that’s a little immature?
Her voice becomes much more stern, clearly displeased by your insensitivity.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: I mean, look at how defeated Rowan looks over there.
You glance over to see how Rowan is hanging his head in shame. Your eyes convey your shame for being so audacious.
Gemini lets out a large sigh.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Well, fine. I guess you’re just new and curious about him. Well, if you really want to know more about him, you should ask him yourself.
You nod, acknowledging your mistake. She side-eyes you, but lets this transgression go for now, though she marks it down mentally.
Rowan endures a dressing down from Professor Hermit. You wait for them to finish before lending a hand to Rowan.

chemistry.name: Professor Hermit
chemistry.text: What you just grabbed was potassium. And you know what happens when you put potassium into a solution that has water?

chemistry.name: Rowan
chemistry.text: It... explodes?

chemistry.name: Professor Hermit
chemistry.text: Yes, Rowan, it does, and surprisingly, it seems that was the first thing you’ve learned about in chemistry in a long time.

chemistry.name: Professor Hermit
chemistry.text: But… considering you’re the pride and glory of our football team… I guess I’ll let you off with another warning. But next time, things won’t go well, ok?

chemistry.name: Rowan
chemistry.text: Yes, professor...
The Professor leaves the table, and Rowan hangs his head over the table, sulking. His cheeks are red with embarrassment.
You and Gemini approach the table to help him.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Hey, Rowan, sorry things didn’t work out. Is everything alright?

chemistry.name: Rowan
chemistry.text: No, it’s ok. I think it’s best if you leave me alone. I’m feeling out of it right now.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: For what it’s worth… I thought you had a great scientific mindset…
You struggle to hear Gemini’s nervous muttering.

chemistry.name: Rowan
chemistry.text: What was that?

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Umm, nothing, just good luck…
Afterwards, you both decide it's best not to bug Rowan anymore as you take your leave back to your table.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Oh, that’s right. Our lab reports are soaked now, huh? Well, it’s just the first day, and the lab was pretty simple. I’m pretty soaked, though, but I’ll dry out.
Gemini takes off her glasses and starts cleaning them. You suddenly notice how beautiful she is, but that’s probably because the smoke from Rowan’s explosion has finally cleared from the room.
RING RING RING RING

chemistry.name: Professor Hermit
chemistry.text: Well, wow, I guess that’s all the time we have. I know everyone’s reports got soaked, so you don’t have to worry about turning them in today.

chemistry.name: Professor Hermit
chemistry.text: You won’t have any homework today either, so I’ll see you next class. Hope you all have a good rest of the day. And… stay safe, ok? Rowan, can we talk for a bit?
You follow Gemini and several other students out of the classroom. Students are chatting with each other, seemingly unfazed by the explosion.
Ahead, you notice Gemini steal a glance behind at Rowan with a worried expression on her face.
In the hallway, Gemini waits for you.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: What class do you have next?
You tell her your schedule.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: Oh, I’ve also got history next. Well then, since you’re new, I can show you the way. I might be a first-year, but I know these halls pretty well because of my friend.
You follow her down the hallways.

chemistry.name: Gemini
chemistry.text: The classroom is actually right next to the courtyard, so why don’t we spend a little time outside in the sun to dry off?
You spend some time outside together. You feel the sun hit your wet clothing, quickly drying them out in a few moments. A short while later, you head to history.
